Override POSTGRES_PASSWORD and NEO4J_PASSWORD before any real deployment.

controls.name: Employee access regularly reviewed
controls.description: Access rights are reviewed at least annually.
controls.detail: The platform records access reviews when they are run, but none has been logged yet.

The mechanism exists; the periodic operation is the agency's.

controls.name: Key inventory maintained
controls.description: An inventory of shared and production access tokens is kept.
controls.detail: Every credential in use is inventoried, but the API bearer token is the username itself — deliberately minimal, and not deployable as-is.
observations: app_user rows are the full inventory of API identities.
Service credentials: the Postgres DSN and Neo4j auth, both from environment.
GAP BY DESIGN: the token carries no secret. Production must terminate on the agency's SSO/PKI; tracex_api.auth.get_principal is shaped as the single seam that changes, so routers stay untouched.

controls.name: Data deletion enforced
controls.description: Data is securely deleted when no longer needed.
controls.detail: Case workspace data is deletable; ingested evidence deliberately is not.
observations: Cases cascade-delete their pinned entities and notes.
ingested_record is append-only on purpose: a hash chain that permits silent deletion is not tamper-evident. Removing a row breaks the chain, and /integrity/verify reports exactly where.
TENSION, STATED: retention-driven erasure therefore means disposing of a whole batch and recording the disposal, not editing rows. That procedure is the agency's to write.

controls.name: Data encrypted in-transit
controls.description: Data is encrypted across internal and external networks.
controls.detail: No plaintext non-local origin is configured, but the app serves HTTP and relies on a TLS terminator in front of it.
observations: CORS origins: https://tracex-web.onrender.com, http://localhost:3000, http://127.0.0.1:3000
Inter-service traffic runs on a private container network.

controls.name: Key management process implemented
controls.description: Cryptographic keys are managed across their lifecycle.
controls.detail: Hashing needs no keys; the service credentials that do exist come from environment configuration with no rotation mechanism.
observations: SHA-256 chaining is keyless, so there is no signing key to steal — the trade-off is that the chain proves integrity, not origin.
Postgres and Neo4j credentials are injected from environment.
GAP: development defaults ship in config. A real deployment must override every one and rotate on a schedule.

controls.name: Data recovery process established
controls.description: A documented process restores data after loss or corruption.
controls.detail: The recovery path is short and documented: restore Postgres, then rebuild the graph from it.
observations: Neo4j is fully derivable from Postgres, so it never needs its own restore.
Writing and owning the runbook step is the agency's.

controls.name: Production and test environments separated
controls.description: Test activity cannot reach production data.
controls.detail: Running in demo mode: the tamper drill is enabled, so this instance must be treated as non-production.
observations: TRACEX_DEMO_MODE=true permits /integrity/drill to mutate a stored record. Correct for a demonstration, unacceptable for an instance holding real evidence.
Set TRACEX_DEMO_MODE=false in production; the drill then refuses.
seed_on_boot=True

controls.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF) used
controls.description: A WAF protects the application from common web attacks.
controls.detail: No WAF is deployed in front of the application; the injection class a WAF usually catches is closed at the source instead.
observations: Every Cypher query is parameterised and covered by a contract test.
Relational access goes through the ORM.
A WAF remains advisable at the perimeter and is the agency's to add.

controls.name: Infrastructure performance monitored

controls.detail: Liveness of every backing service is exposed at /health; there is no metrics history or alerting.
observations: Postgres, Neo4j and the LLM provider are each probed.
The UI degrades honestly when one is down rather than showing a blank panel that reads as 'no findings'.

controls.name: Log management used

controls.name: Threat intelligence established

controls.name: Non-conformance and corrective action procedures established

controls.name: Offboarding process established
controls.description: Departing staff lose access promptly.
controls.detail: Removing an app_user row revokes all access immediately, because identity is resolved against that table on every request.
observations: No session or token survives the removal — there is nothing to expire.
Triggering offboarding on a leaver is the agency's process.

controls.name: Onboarding process established
controls.description: New staff receive appropriate access.
controls.detail: Access begins with an explicit provisioning act — a row with a named role — and never by default.
observations: An unprovisioned identity is rejected, so 'forgot to set permissions' fails closed rather than open.

controls.name: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) completed

Explainability: every risk score ships its own attribution, so an adverse inference can be contested.
Exculpatory surfacing: the report generator carries evidence that cuts against the hypothesis, not only for it.
A signed DPIA remains the agency's to complete.

controls.name: Penetration testing findings remediated
controls.description: Findings from penetration tests are fixed.
controls.detail: no penetration test has been performed, so there are no findings to remediate; the missing test itself is reported at CTL-VLN-003

controls.name: Access granting process used
controls.description: New access is granted on least privilege, with each grant attributable.
controls.detail: 2 users provisioned, every one holding a defined role; 5 actions are restricted to supervisors.
observations: roles in use: investigator, supervisor
privileged actions: case.action_withdrawn, case.close, case.freeze_request, case.sar_draft, evidence.package.export
Access is granted by provisioning a row in app_user; an unprovisioned identity is rejected at the door with 401.

controls.name: Access management policy established
controls.description: Systematic controls govern user access rights to systems and data.
controls.detail: Access rules are enforced server-side in tracex_api.auth, not in the UI.
observations: Two roles: investigator (read, ingest, analyse, work cases) and supervisor (all of that, plus closure, export, and any action with an external consequence).
The frontend hides privileged controls as a convenience; the API refuses them as the control. A hidden button is not a permission.
5 privileged actions declared.

controls.name: Dedicated administrator accounts used
controls.description: Elevated privileges are confined to dedicated accounts.
controls.detail: 1 of 2 users hold supervisor rights; the rest operate unprivileged.
observations: supervisors: supervisor

controls.name: Data inventory maintained
controls.description: An accurate inventory of data assets is maintained.
controls.detail: Live inventory across 5 source type(s), 2119 records total — derived from storage, not maintained by hand.
observations: alpr: 140 records across 1 batch(es)
bank: 407 records across 1 batch(es)
cdr: 1119 records across 1 batch(es)
ipdr: 449 records across 1 batch(es)
social: 4 records across 1 batch(es)
Every row records its source file, batch, ingest time and ingesting user.

controls.name: Data labeled according to classification level
controls.description: Data carries a classification that drives its handling.
controls.detail: Every record is classified by source type at ingest and carries that label for its whole life.
observations: classes present: alpr, bank, cdr, ipdr, social
The label drives handling: source type selects the parser, the graph projection, and which analyses may read the row.

controls.name: Data masking procedures used
controls.description: Non-production environments do not contain live sensitive data.
controls.detail: Non-production data is synthetic, not masked production data.
observations: The seed corpus is generated, so there is no real subject to re-identify.
This is the stronger form of the control: masking can be undone by correlation, and synthetic data has nothing to be undone to.

controls.name: Data processing integrity and output validated
controls.description: Processing is complete, accurate and tamper-evident end to end.
controls.detail: All 2119 records across 5 batch(es) re-hashed and every chain re-walked; no discrepancy.
observations: This is a full re-hash of stored payloads, not a link-only check — the latter would miss an edit made directly in the database.
The same check is exposed at /integrity/verify, and /integrity/drill will break it on demand so the verifier can be watched catching it.

controls.name: Data transfer mechanisms established
controls.description: Data leaves the system only through controlled, audited paths.
controls.detail: Evidence leaves the system only through the export path, which is supervisor-gated, hash-certified and audited.
observations: 5 export-related audit entries recorded.
Exports carry a BSA s.65B-style certificate binding the package to the hash chain it was drawn from.
No outbound egress: the LLM provider is local (stub or Ollama) and no cloud API is called.

controls.name: Administrator access restricted
controls.description: Elevated permissions are granted narrowly and revoked promptly.
controls.detail: Elevated actions are enumerated and enforced at the API boundary.
observations: Restricted: case.action_withdrawn, case.close, case.freeze_request, case.sar_draft, evidence.package.export

Each one has an external consequence — closing a case, exporting evidence, asking a bank to freeze funds, filing a regulatory report. Read and analysis are unrestricted, because an investigator who cannot look at the data cannot investigate.

controls.name: Clock synchronization enforced
controls.description: System clocks are synchronised to a reliable source.
controls.detail: Every timestamp the application writes is timezone-aware UTC, taken from the host clock.
observations: Records, audit entries and case events all use datetime.now(dt.UTC).
This matters evidentially: a timeline correlating CDR, banking and social events across sources is only sound if all of them are on one clock. Host NTP remains the agency's to maintain.

controls.name: Configuration management system established
controls.description: Configuration is managed and version-controlled.
controls.detail: All runtime configuration is environment-driven through a single typed settings object, with defaults visible in source.
observations: No configuration is read from an unversioned host file.
A reviewer can see which values produced a given verdict — analysis thresholds are echoed in the responses that used them.

controls.name: Audit log management process maintained
controls.description: Audit logs are captured, retained and reviewable.
controls.detail: The audit log is append-only in application code and queryable through a filtered, paginated route.
observations: No route updates or deletes an audit row.
Indexed on timestamp, actor and action so a review is practical, not theoretical.

LIMIT, STATED: append-only is enforced by the application, not the database. A holder of direct database credentials could still edit it; the ingested-record hash chain is what defends the evidence itself.

controls.name: Audit logs collected
controls.description: Security-relevant events are logged from critical components.
controls.detail: 170 audit entries from 4 distinct actor(s), across 8+ action types.
observations: timeline.entity.view: 42
intel.analyze: 24
intel.entity.view: 23
spatial.reconstruct: 13
spatial.layers: 13
ask.query: 12
benchmark.run: 6
hunt.sweep: 6
The actor is derived from the request identity, never accepted as a client-supplied field — an audit log the caller can forge is decoration.

controls.name: Compliance monitoring processes defined and implemented
controls.description: Control effectiveness is monitored on an ongoing basis.
controls.detail: Compliance posture is computed from the live system on request, not maintained as a spreadsheet.
observations: Every control in this catalogue carries a verifier that inspects the running deployment; results are recomputed on each call.
Controls nothing can verify are reported as unclaimed rather than assumed to pass, and they lower the readiness score.

controls.name: Data-flow diagrams maintained
controls.description: Data flows across systems are documented and current.
controls.detail: The data flow is documented and, more usefully, inspectable at runtime.
observations: Ingest -> hash chain -> entity resolution -> graph projection -> analysis -> case -> certified export.
Each stage is a named service module, and the agent pipeline view renders the actual path a record took rather than an idealised drawing.

controls.name: Roles and responsibilities specified
controls.description: Duties and accountabilities are defined.
controls.detail: Two roles are defined with explicit duties, and the boundary between them is enforced rather than described.

controls.name: Scope for compliance framework established
controls.description: The boundary of the framework is defined.
controls.detail: Scope is declared explicitly and every control is attributed to an owner inside or outside it.
observations: In scope: the TRACE-X application, its two datastores, and the evidence lifecycle from ingest to certified export.
Out of scope: the agency's corporate estate — email, endpoints, network, premises and HR. Those controls are listed and marked, never silently dropped, so the boundary itself is auditable.

controls.name: Service description communicated
controls.description: Scope, features and limitations are communicated to users.
controls.detail: The service, its scope and its stated limits are documented in-product.
observations: OpenAPI at /docs; every analytical view states its method and its caveats.

controls.name: Statement of applicability completed
controls.description: Applicable controls are formally identified.
controls.detail: This catalogue is the statement of applicability: every control is present with an owner, a status and its justification.
observations: 125 controls across 10 domains.
Exclusions carry a stated reason rather than an omission.
